title: DNS Record Guard
summary: Checks a DNS edit or delete against the whole zone before saving, so a removed MX or broken SPF doesn't quietly stop company email.
description: Checks a DNS change against the zone: a removed MX, SPF senders dropped or past the 10-lookup limit, a removed DKIM selector (escalated under enforcing DMARC), a CNAME at the root or beside other records and dangling names, then says how long it takes to spread.
catches: Removing MX records that receive company email
SPF senders dropped, or SPF pushed past the 10 DNS-lookup limit
A DKIM selector removed while DMARC enforces
A CNAME at the zone root or beside other records, and names left pointing at nothing
Long TTLs, with "lower TTL first" and a countdown until caches clear
limits: Checks only the records you pass; it doesn't query live DNS
Can't know which third-party senders still need SPF or DKIM
a11y: Dialog content is labelled by its title
Findings are aria-live="polite" and say "Breaks:" or "Risk:" in text
The TTL countdown is aria-live="polite"; its progress bar is aria-hidden
server: Validate zone changes at your DNS provider and keep a record of the previous zone so changes can be rolled back.

sources.label: RFC 2181: CNAME may have no other data

rules.note: Informational. Checked the SPF limit of 10 lookup terms and that a CNAME label may hold no other data. DKIM/DMARC escalation rules were not checked against a standard.

stops: Deleted MX record stopped company email
